answers.answer: Shuffle the nine region cards, reveal one for the King’s region, and give each player another to set their home region and place their Grande. Each gets ten Caballeros: two beside the Grande in home, one on the first success-track space, and seven in their court.
answers.evidence: Setup: reveal the top region card for the King; each player takes another for home. Ten: two home, one on success track, seven in court.

answers.answer: Players choose the round 1 starter. In later rounds, the player who took the last turn in the preceding round starts playing power cards; the others play clockwise. No value already played that round may be matched.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure 2: chosen starter in round 1; later, last-turn player begins; others clockwise; no value already played may be matched.

answers.answer: Turns are in descending power-card value. At the start of your turn, recruit up to the Caballero allowance pictured on the power card from provinces to court (you may recruit fewer). This happens before choosing an available action card.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure 3–4: ‘At the start of your turn recruit up to’ the pictured number; after recruitment, choose an action card.

answers.answer: If your provinces lack enough of your color, you may take your own Caballeros from the board to make up the difference. The King’s region and Castillo cannot supply the pieces.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure 3: may take your own from the board; King’s region remains taboo and Castillo cannot supply pieces outside general scoring.

answers.answer: Ordinary deployment is from court to regions adjacent to the King’s current region and/or the Castillo, dividing the allowance freely. It may be split among destinations. The printed number is a maximum, so you may deploy fewer or none.
answers.evidence: Ordinary deployment: ‘maximum’; ‘Move them from your court to any regions adjacent to the King’s current region and/or the Castillo, dividing the allowance freely.’

answers.answer: Yes. Complete ordinary deployment and the special action in either order, but complete each activity before starting the other; neither can be interleaved. The special action may be declined.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure 4: do them ‘in either order’ but ‘neither may be split or interleaved’; may decline the special action.

answers.answer: After a turn, lay the selected action card aside so later players cannot choose it. At round end discard remaining face-up action cards. The King card is revealed again every round and is never permanently discarded.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure 5: selected card laid aside; remaining face-up cards discarded; King card revealed again every round and never permanently discarded.

answers.answer: No Caballero, Grande, or mobile scoreboard may move into or out of the King’s region. It may still be scored. Moving the King changes which region is protected.
answers.evidence: Protected locations: King’s region is taboo for Caballero, Grande, or mobile scoreboard movement; it may still be scored; moving the King changes protected region.

answers.answer: Announce clearly how many Caballeros you put in the Castillo. Entry is allowed regardless of the King’s location. They cannot leave through an action; they leave only during general scoring.
answers.evidence: Protected locations: ‘Announce clearly how many you put inside’; any or all may go into Castillo regardless of King; leave only during general scoring.

answers.answer: After rounds 3, 6, and 9: (1) before uncovering the Castillo, each player secretly sets a disk to one board region other than the King’s region; all their Castillo pieces go to that one region. (2) Score the Castillo. (3) Reveal disks and move each player’s pieces there, emptying the Castillo. (4) Score the nine regions in scoring-track order. Destinations are chosen before revealing the Castillo.
answers.evidence: General scoring stages 1–4; timing is ‘after rounds 3, 6 and 9’; destination choice occurs before uncovering the Castillo.

answers.answer: A player cannot split their Castillo Caballeros: all go to one destination. They cannot legally choose the King’s region and cannot keep pieces in the Castillo. If they illegally selected the King’s region, those pieces go to that player’s court. Otherwise the Castillo is emptied into the selected region.
answers.evidence: General scoring: ‘all’ Castillo Caballeros go to ‘one’ region; King’s region prohibited; illegal selection sends pieces to court; none may be retained or split.

answers.answer: The three players tied with four score 3 points each; the player with three scores 1. Grandes do not count toward majority.
answers.evidence: Example on 5/3/1: counts 4,4,4,3 score 3,3,3,1; only Caballeros count, a Grande contributes zero.

answers.answer: The players with 4 and 3 score 6 and 4 respectively; both players with 2 score 0 because they tie for third and drop to fourth place.
answers.evidence: Example on 6/4/2: counts 4,3,2,2 score 6,4,0,0; tie for third drops to fourth and scores zero.

answers.answer: In a two-player game, only first place can pay; in a three-player game, first and second can pay. A two-player tie for first takes the next rank’s value (second), which is outside the two-player payable ranks, so both score zero.
answers.evidence: Region ranks: two players only first can pay; three players first and second; apply player-count cutoff after rank shift, so a two-player tie for first pays neither.

answers.answer: Whenever the relevant region is scored, including special scoring, the sole majority holder in the King’s region gets +2 and the sole majority holder with their own Grande in that region gets +2. Neither bonus is awarded on a tie for first.
answers.evidence: Bonuses apply whenever region scored, including special scorings; each is +2 for sole majority; neither on a tie.

answers.answer: Special scoring reveals and scores the Castillo’s contents, then covers those same pieces again. It does not empty or redistribute them; redistribution waits until general scoring.
answers.evidence: Stack 3: score Castillo, then cover the same Caballeros; redistribution waits until general scoring.

answers.answer: A mobile scoreboard may be placed at the Castillo. It cannot move into or out of the King’s region, cannot be stacked on the other scoreboard, and must stay right side up as 8/4/0 or 4/0/0; it cannot be rotated to create other values.
answers.evidence: Stack 4: Castillo allowed; no movement into/out of King’s region; scoreboards cannot be stacked; place right side up and never reverse or rotate.

answers.answer: Move your Grande to another region, but not into the King’s region or Castillo; it cannot leave the King’s region. The destination may already contain any number of other Grandes. The destination becomes your new home region.
answers.evidence: Stack 4 Grande: move to another region except King’s region or Castillo; cannot leave King’s region; destination may contain several Grandes; it becomes new home.

answers.answer: Return any one of your played power cards to your hand, including the card played this turn. You need not reveal which card you choose, although taking the visible top card will be apparent.
answers.evidence: Stack 4 Power Cards: any one played card, including this turn’s; need not reveal which; visible top card is apparent.

answers.answer: The game ends after completing all stages of the third general scoring, after round 9. The player furthest along the success track wins. No additional tiebreaker is given.
answers.evidence: End: finish third general scoring after round 9; furthest along success track wins; no additional tiebreaker.

answers.answer: Separate action cards into stacks by the 1–5 Caballeros printed on their backs, shuffle each stack separately, and place face down. Reveal the top card of each of the five stacks at the start of every round. The standard round marker starts at 1.
answers.evidence: Setup: stacks by 1–5, shuffled separately; standard marker at 1. Turn Structure: reveal top card of each five action stacks each round.

answers.answer: Played power cards are not returned to hand. They remain in each player’s face-up used stack with only the top card visible; a special action can recover a played card.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure 2: played cards remain in face-up used stack, only top visible; a special action can recover a played card.

answers.answer: If the King is moved before ordinary deployment, the King’s new position determines adjacent destinations; if deployment happens first, use his old position. The King card may place him in any region except the Castillo.
answers.evidence: Protected locations: if King moved before deployment, use new position. Stack 5: put King in any region except Castillo.

answers.answer: Retain the Veto card in front of you. It can stop one special action during this round or the next, but it cannot stop the ordinary deployment portion of an action card.
answers.evidence: Stack 2 Veto: put card before you and retain it to stop one special action; cannot stop ordinary deployment.

answers.answer: While Veto is held, other players must announce special actions before executing them. Object as soon as the player starts: you can stop an announced action before execution or prevent the remaining part of an incomplete action. A completed action cannot be vetoed; a partial veto does not undo parts already executed.
answers.evidence: Veto: announce special actions; object as soon as player starts; stop before execution or prevent remaining incomplete action; completed actions cannot be vetoed and executed parts are not undone.

answers.answer: Discard Veto after using it once. If unused, discard it at the end of the next round.
answers.evidence: Veto: ‘Discard after using the veto once; if unused, discard at the end of the next round.’

answers.answer: Every fellow player sends all Caballeros in their court to the provinces; the selecting player is unaffected. A player with an empty court sends none.
answers.evidence: Decay of Authority — all court: every fellow player sends all court Caballeros to provinces; empty court sends none; selector unaffected.

answers.answer: The fellow player with two sends both to the provinces (‘all they have if fewer than three’); the selecting player with five is unaffected and keeps them.
answers.evidence: Decay — three from court: each fellow player sends three or all if fewer than three; selecting player unaffected.

answers.answer: The detailed execution paragraph says each player, including the selecting player, sends three of their own Caballeros to the provinces. Starting with the player to the selector’s left, proceed clockwise, selector last. Pieces may come from any regions and/or court, never the King’s region or Castillo. The source gives no shortfall rule if fewer than three eligible pieces exist. The heading instead says ‘fellow players.’
answers.evidence: The King returns detailed paragraph and card say each player, including selector, three; left then clockwise, selector last; sources any regions/court except King/Castillo; heading conflicts by saying fellow players.

answers.answer: The selecting player chooses one Caballero from a region for each player, including themselves, and returns each piece to its owner’s provinces. The selecting player therefore loses one too. Pieces cannot be taken from courts, the King’s region, or the Castillo. No fallback is stated if a player has no eligible piece.
answers.evidence: Send one from each player: selecting player chooses one for each player including themselves; no courts, King’s region or Castillo; no explicit fallback for no eligible piece.

answers.answer: Each affected fellow player secretly chooses one region on their disk; choices are simultaneous and revealed together. The selected region must contain at least two of that player’s Caballeros, and two are returned to the provinces. If they have a legal region with at least two, they must choose a region meeting that requirement; the summary does not prescribe which qualifying region.
answers.evidence: Fellow players secretly remove two: simultaneous secret disk selection, reveal together; choose region with at least two of that player’s Caballeros; return two.

answers.answer: If the player has at most one Caballero in every region, they choose a region containing one and return that one Caballero to the provinces.
answers.evidence: The stated singleton fallback applies if the player has at most one in every region: choose a region with one and return that one.

answers.answer: Each affected fellow player secretly chooses a region containing at least one of their Caballeros, with disk choices revealed together, and returns all their own Caballeros there to the provinces. A player with none in any region is unaffected.
answers.evidence: Secretly remove all from one region: simultaneous secret disk selection; region must have at least one; return all their own there; player with none is unaffected.

answers.answer: Yes, choose any region, including the King’s region or the Castillo. Use normal region-scoring rules, including applicable rank limits and bonuses. If Castillo is selected, score and cover the same pieces again; do not redistribute them.
answers.evidence: Choose any region includes King’s region or Castillo; normal scoring; Castillo scored and same pieces covered again without redistribution.

answers.answer: The printed 4-value group is Galicia (4/2/0), Catalonia (4/2/1), and Seville (4/3/1). Eligibility uses the current first value, including a mobile scoreboard: Galicia with 8/4/0 does not qualify, while Granada with 4/0/0 does. Applicable bonuses apply to special scorings.
answers.evidence: All 4-value regions: current first value is 4; printed group listed; mobile 8/4/0 removes Galicia and 4/0/0 adds Granada. Bonuses apply including special scorings.

answers.answer: The printed 5-value group is Basque Country (5/3/1), Aragon (5/4/1), Valencia (5/3/2). The printed 6-and-7 group is Old Castile (6/4/2), New Castile (7/4/2), Granada (6/3/1). For both groups, eligibility follows the current first value, so mobile scoreboards can change which regions qualify. Castillo is expressly excluded from all-5 scoring.
answers.evidence: All 5-value: current first value 5 and Castillo not scored; all 6/7: current first value 6 or 7. Mobile scoreboard replaces printed values for category eligibility.

answers.answer: Only sole first-place players score; a tie for first scores nothing because it would normally receive second-place value. All lower ranks score nothing. Castillo is excluded.
answers.evidence: First-position-only: only sole first places score; tie for first scores nothing; other ranks get nothing; excludes Castillo.

answers.answer: Score every board region tied for the most total Caballeros. Do not consider or score the Castillo, even if it contains more than either region.
answers.evidence: Most Caballeros: score all regions tied for most; Castillo is neither considered nor scored.

answers.answer: Compare nonempty board regions and score every region tied for the least. Empty regions and Castillo are not considered or scored.
answers.evidence: Least Caballeros: compare nonempty board regions; score all tied for least; empty regions and Castillo neither considered nor scored.

answers.answer: All fellow players move all their own Caballeros out of the chosen region. Each affected player secretly selects another region on their disk; choices are revealed simultaneously and that player’s whole group moves there. If they choose the King’s region or the region being vacated, their pieces go to their court instead. The summary flags an unresolved conflict: general rules allow entry to Castillo, but the Movement card’s disk omits Castillo; it does not provide a definitive procedure for that case.
answers.evidence: Movement card: fellow players move all their own pieces; secret disk choice; King’s region or vacated region sends group to court. Edge cases note no reconciliation for Castillo with Movement-card disks.

answers.answer: Royal Adviser moves the King at most one region, to a neighboring region. The King card can move him to any region except the Castillo.
answers.evidence: Royal Adviser: neighboring region, no more than one region away. King card: any region except Castillo.

answers.answer: The Court special action moves two of your own Caballeros from provinces to your court. This is separate from the 4-stack card’s ordinary deployment of up to four from court to the board; complete the two activities separately, in either order.
answers.evidence: The Court: two own from provinces to court; separate from ordinary up-to-four court-to-board deployment; either activity can go first.

answers.answer: All players secretly choose a region on their disks and reveal simultaneously. Score each uniquely selected region under normal rules; a region selected by multiple players is not scored. The disk includes the King’s region but excludes the Castillo.
answers.evidence: Each secretly chooses a region: all choose secretly and reveal simultaneously; unique choices score, duplicate choices do not; disk includes King’s region, not Castillo.

answers.answer: You may move all your own Caballeros from one region and distribute them among other regions and/or Castillo, and may return some to the original region. Origins exclude the King’s region and Castillo; destinations exclude the King’s region but may include Castillo.
answers.evidence: Intrigue all-own effect permits distribution and expressly returning some to original; origins exclude King and Castillo; destinations exclude King, may include Castillo.

answers.answer: The special action adds up to two additional own Caballeros from court to any non-King region(s) and/or Castillo. Combined with normal deployment, up to three may enter the board; only the normal one is restricted to regions adjacent to the King’s current region and/or Castillo.
answers.evidence: Intrigue ‘Two more from court’: up to two additional to any non-King regions and/or Castillo; with normal one, up to three; only normal one requires adjacency.

answers.answer: No. Choose one of the two special alternatives, not both: either two additional from court or all your own from one region. The normal up-to-one deployment remains available.
answers.evidence: Intrigue choice card: choose one preceding special action, not both; normal deployment still applies.

answers.answer: Move up to five Caballeros, of your own and/or other players’ ownership, from one origin region only. Distribute them to other non-King regions and/or Castillo; multiple origin regions are not allowed. The King’s region and Castillo cannot be origins.
answers.evidence: Intrigue ‘Up to five from one region’: own and/or foreign, one origin, to other non-King regions and/or Castillo; origins exclude King and Castillo.

answers.answer: You may move up to three foreign Caballeros, from any number of non-King board-region origins; Castillo cannot be a source and your own Caballeros cannot be included. Destinations may be any non-King regions and/or Castillo.
answers.evidence: Intrigue ‘Any three foreign’: up to three other players’ pieces from any non-King board regions, multiple origins, never Castillo; destinations any non-King regions and/or Castillo.

answers.answer: ‘Any three’ allows up to three own and/or foreign Caballeros from any non-King origin regions to any non-King regions and/or Castillo. ‘Any four’ allows up to four own and/or foreign from any non-King origins into other non-King regions and/or Castillo. Castillo is never a source; the four-piece card says ‘other’ regions for destinations.
answers.evidence: Intrigue table distinguishes any three (any non-King regions) from any four (other non-King regions); all table entries subject to Castillo and King taboo.

answers.answer: The allowances are up to two of your own plus up to two foreign Caballeros (separate ownership limits), from any number of eligible origin regions. Sources cannot be the King’s region or Castillo. Destinations may be any non-King regions and/or Castillo.
answers.evidence: Intrigue: ‘two own and two foreign’ are separate ownership allowances; multi-origin movement; table entries subject to taboo and Castillo rules.

answers.answer: Move up to four Caballeros, your own only, from any non-King origin regions into other non-King regions and/or Castillo. Castillo cannot be a source.
answers.evidence: Intrigue ‘Any four of your own’: up to four own only, from any non-King origin regions into other non-King regions and/or Castillo; global rule prohibits Castillo sources.

answers.answer: The each-player secret scoring card’s disks allow the nine board regions, including the King’s region, but not Castillo; unique selections score and duplicates do not. This differs from the acting player’s ‘choose any region’ card, which allows King’s region or Castillo and scores that chosen location.
answers.evidence: Stack 4: secret choice disk includes King’s region but not Castillo; Stack 3 choose any region includes King’s region or Castillo.

answers.answer: Both mobile scoreboards begin beside the board. The place-or-move action may introduce one from beside the board or move one already on the board to a different region.
answers.evidence: Setup: place both mobile scoreboards beside the board. Stack 4 mobile scoreboard action: introduce one from beside the board or move one already on it to a different region.
